chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is amiable (gets acquainted with others), and there is no good in the one who neither gets acquainted nor is gotten acquainted with.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.مَأْلُوفٌ: Amiable / Socially approachable / One who forms bonds
key_terms.يُؤْلَفُ: Is gotten acquainted with / Is approached by others

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be 'ma'luf' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Sahih al-Kulayni, highlights the Prophetic tradition of *al-mu'allafah qulubuhum* (softening hearts) by illustrating that social cohesion is a hallmark of faith. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *sulh* (reconciliation) and approachability as essential traits for maintaining communal harmony, contrasting the believer with the isolated individual who lacks spiritual and social grace.
